name: Slider
description: A control for choosing a value, or a range between two values, by dragging a handle along a track. It's a native range input, so the keyboard, forms and screen readers work as usual.

classes.ayy-slider--lg: Thicker 8px track and a 24px thumb, in a medium control tall box.
classes.ayy-slider-range--sm: A range with the small track and thumb; sizes both inputs inside it.
classes.ayy-slider-range--lg: A range with the large track and thumb; sizes both inputs inside it.
classes.ayy-slider: On <input type="range">. --ayy-value (0–100, where the value sits between min and max) fills the track up to the thumb; React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements keep it in sync, so in HTML set the starting one inline.
classes.ayy-slider-range: A role="group" around two .ayy-slider inputs (the min, then the max) sharing one track, filled between --ayy-from and --ayy-to (0–100). @danitesler/ayywi/elements keeps them in sync and stops the thumbs crossing.

default.looks: A 6px pill track in a 14% text tint, filled in the text colour up to an 18px page-coloured thumb with a text-colour rim.

pressed.none: No separate pressed look; the thumb follows the pointer while dragged.

focus.looks: Ring around the thumb (page-colour gap, then 2px ring), not the track.

selected.none: The value is the state: the fill reaches it (--ayy-value 0–100).

error.none: A slider can't hold an invalid value; its min, max and step bound it.

scale.sm: 4px track, 14px thumb, in the sm control height box (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch).
scale.md: 6px track, 18px thumb, in the sm control height box.
scale.lg: 8px track, 24px thumb, in the md control height box (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).

sizes.density: The control box follows data-density; track and thumb are fixed.
sizes.width: Fills its container. A range (two thumbs) is .ayy-slider-range.

js: sliderPercent(input) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; syncSlider(input) updates --ayy-value (or the range's --ayy-from / --ayy-to and keeps the thumbs from crossing). @danitesler/ayywi/elements runs it on every input event; call it after setting a value from code. sliderClass, sliderRangeClass constants; sliderSizeClass(size?, range = false) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for a slider, or a range when range is true; md adds nothing).

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (the native size attribute is not exposed)

SliderRange.renders: <div role="group" class="ayy-slider-range"> with two range inputs

props.labels: [string, string] — the thumbs' names ("Minimum price", "Maximum price")

a11y: It's a native range input: arrow keys step, Page Up/Down jump, Home/End go to the ends, and screen readers read the value. Give it a <label> (or aria-label); add aria-valuetext when the number needs a unit ("12 people").
Show the value in text next to the label (an <output>), so it doesn't depend on the thumb's position.
Each thumb of a range has its own name ("Minimum price", "Maximum price"); name the group with aria-labelledby.
The focus ring is on the thumb. In High Contrast the fill and the thumb take system colours.
do: Use a slider for a value where roughly is fine and the range is small: a class size, a volume, a radius, a budget.
Use a range slider to filter by price or size between a min and a max.
Pick a step that matches what people choose (5, 10, 0.5), and print the value next to the label.
dont: Don't use a slider when people need an exact number — use an Input (type number) or a Number field.
Don't use it for a choice between a few named options — use a Segmented control or Radio buttons.
Don't hide what min and max mean: label the ends or the value.
